results.title: Right-invariant linear order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A linear order $\le$ on a group $G$ is right-invariant (a right order) when $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.

results.title: Right-relatively convex subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is right-relatively convex when there is a right-invariant linear order $\le$ on $G$ for which $H$ is convex: whenever $h_1 \le g \le h_2$ with $h_1, h_2 \in H$ and $g \in G$, also $g \in H$.

results.title: Sublattice question for right-relatively convex subgroups (Kourovka Problem 21.147, non-abelian case)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Sublattice question for right-relatively convex subgroups (Kourovka Problem 21.147, non-abelian case). The statement that for every non-abelian right-orderable group $G$ and all right-relatively convex subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$, both the intersection $H \cap K$ and the join $H \vee K$ (the subgroup generated by $H$ and $K$) are right-relatively convex; that is, the right-relatively convex subgroups of $G$ form a…

results.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 21.147 for non-abelian groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that for every non-abelian right-orderable group $G$ and all right-relatively convex subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$, both the intersection $H \cap K$ and the join $H \vee K$ (the subgroup generated by $H$ and $K$) are right-relatively convex.

results.title: Quasi-identities of groups
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A quasi-identity consists of a natural number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all elements of the free group $F_n$ on the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. It stands for the formula $\forall x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}\, (w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$.

results.title: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a quasi-identity with unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and conclusion $w$, all in the free group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. For $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ in a group $G$ and $u \in F_n$, write $u(g_0, \dots, g_{n-1})$ for the image of $u$ under the homomorphism $F_n \to G$ sending each $x_j$ to $g_j$. Then $q$ holds in $G$ when for all $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1} \in G$ with…

results.title: Closure of a set of words with respect to a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $F_n$ be the free group on the basis $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, and let $T \subseteq F_n$. The $G$-closure $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the set of $w \in F_n$ such that $\mu(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism $\mu : F_n \to G$ with $\mu(t) = 1$ for all $t \in T$, that is, the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.

results.title: Geometrically equivalent groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ are geometrically equivalent (B. I. Plotkin) when $\mathrm{cl}_G(T) = \mathrm{cl}_H(T)$ for every natural number $n$ and every subset $T$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, where $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the $G$-closure of $T$: the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.

results.title: Plotkin's problem on quasi-identities and geometric equivalence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition (Kourovka Problem 14.71, B. I. Plotkin) that any two groups $G$ and $H$ satisfying the same quasi-identities, meaning that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, are geometrically equivalent.

results.title: Groups with the same quasi-identities need not be geometrically equivalent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 14.71 is false: there are groups $G$ and $H$ such that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, but $G$ and $H$ are not geometrically equivalent.

results.title: Quasivariety generated by a finite group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $K$, a group $X$ lies in the class $Q(K)$ when $X$ embeds in a direct power of $K$: there are a set $I$ and an injective homomorphism $X \to K^I$.

results.title: Join of the quasivarieties generated by two finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $G$ and $H$, a group $X$ lies in the class $Q(G, H)$ when $X$ embeds in the product of a direct power of $G$ and a direct power of $H$: there are sets $I$ and $J$ and an injective homomorphism $X \to G^I \times H^J$.

results.title: Quasivarieties generated by finite $p$-groups need not form a sublattice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For some prime $p$ there are finite $p$-groups $G$ and $H$ such that no finite $p$-group generates the intersection of the quasivarieties generated by $G$ and by $H$, or no finite $p$-group generates their join. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.9 (Budkin) in the negative.

Here $V^{-2}$ and $V^{-4}$ are read as $0$ when $V = 0$.

results.title: Bounded holomorphic functions on the punctured plane are constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$, and suppose that there is a real number $C$ with $|f(z)| \le C$ for every $z \ne 0$. Then there is a constant $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for every $z \ne 0$.

results.title: An entire function with a polynomial derivative is a polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. If there is a complex polynomial $p$ such that the $k$th derivative of $f$ satisfies $f^{(k)}(z) = p(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$, then there is a complex polynomial $q$ such that $f(z) = q(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: An entire function of sublinear growth is constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function such that $f(z)/z \to 0$ as $|z| \to \infty$. Then $f$ is constant: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Existence for the Sturm–Liouville Dirichlet problem on the closed unit interval
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ and $f$ be continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ with $V \ge 0$. Then there is a function $u \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is $C^2$ on $[0, 1]$, satisfies $-u''(x) + V(x)\,u(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$, with the second derivative taken within $[0, 1]$, and has $u(0) = u(1) = 0$.

results.title: Uniqueness for the Sturm–Liouville Dirichlet problem on the closed unit interval
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ and $f$ be continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ with $V \ge 0$, and let $u_1, u_2 \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be $C^2$ on $[0, 1]$. Suppose that for $i = 1, 2$, $-u_i''(x) + V(x)\,u_i(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$, with the second derivative taken within $[0, 1]$, and $u_i(0) = u_i(1) = 0$. Then $u_1$ and $u_2$ agree on $[0, 1]$.

results.title: Existence for the one-dimensional Dirichlet problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[0, 1]$. Then there is a twice continuously differentiable function $u : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $u(0) = u(1) = 0$ and $u''(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in (0, 1)$.

results.title: Uniqueness for the one-dimensional Dirichlet problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be any function, and let $u_1, u_2 : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable functions such that, for $i = 1, 2$, $u_i(0) = u_i(1) = 0$ and $u_i''(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in (0, 1)$. Then $u_1(x) = u_2(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Le Cam's first lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Le Cam's first lemma (LAN case). Let `Qₙ = exp(Λₙ) · P` be probability measures. If `Sₙ → N(0, v)` in distribution under `P` and `Λₙ - h Sₙ → -h² v / 2` in `P`-probability, then `Qₙ` is contiguous with respect to `P`. This is the case of Le Cam's first lemma in which `Λₙ → N(-σ²/2, σ²)` under `P`, `σ² = h² v`; the general form (any limit `L` of `dQₙ/dP` with `E L = 1`) is not stated here.

results.summary: A set-cover instance is a triple $(n, C, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the size of the universe, a finite list $C$ of finite lists of natural numbers, the subsets, and a natural number $K$, the bound.

results.title: Feasible set-cover instances

results.title: Immerman-Szelepcsenyi theorem: NL = coNL
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The complexity class NL is closed under complementation: a decision problem $L$ belongs to NL if and only if its complement, the decision problem that is true exactly on the bitstrings where $L$ is false, belongs to NL.

results.title: Karp-Lipton theorem: NP in P/poly collapses PH
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If every decision problem in NP belongs to P/poly (polynomial time with polynomial advice), then the polynomial hierarchy PH equals its second level $\Sigma_2^p$.

results.title: Ladner's theorem: NP-intermediate languages exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If P $\ne$ NP, then there is a decision problem $L$ in NP that is not in P and to which not every decision problem in NP reduces by a polynomial-time many-one reduction; that is, $L$ is in NP but is neither in P nor NP-complete.

results.title: Savitch's theorem: NPSPACE = PSPACE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The complexity class NPSPACE of decision problems decided in polynomial space by nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machines equals the class PSPACE of decision problems decided in polynomial space by deterministic multi-tape Turing machines.

results.summary: Expected SFS under a variable population size (Griffiths & Tavaré 1998; Polanski & Kimmel 2003). Let the genealogy of a sample of `n` copies consist of holding times `T k` (integrable for `2 ≤ k ≤ n`, otherwise arbitrary) and an independent block-size history `τ` with the random-joining law. If, given the genealogy, the count `ξ i` is integrable with conditional mean `(θ / 2) L_i`, then…

results.title: Variable-size spectrum reduces to Fu's $\theta/i$ at constant size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With the constant-size means `E T_k = 1 / C(k,2)`, the variable-size SFS is Fu's `θ / i`.

reading_title.source: Variable-size spectrum reduces to Fu's $\theta/i$ at constant size

results.title: Griffiths–Tavaré kernel vanishes beyond the diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The kernel row `i` vanishes beyond `k = n - i + 1`: a branch subtending `i` copies cannot exist while more than `n - i + 1` lineages remain.

results.title: Positivity of the Griffiths–Tavaré kernel on the diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The kernel entry at `k = n - i + 1` is `(n - i + 1) / C(n-1, i-1) > 0`.

results.title: The expected SFS determines the mean holding times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two vectors of mean holding times give the same expected SFS for some `θ ≠ 0`, they agree at every `k = 2, …, n`. This is a direct consequence of `sfsKernel_eq_zero_of_lt` and `sfsKernel_diag_pos` (the kernel is triangular with nonzero diagonal); it is recorded here as an observation, not as a cited theorem.

results.title: Achaz's weighted estimator of $\theta$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Achaz's weighted estimator `θ_ω = ∑_{i=1}^{n-1} ω_i i ξ_i` (Achaz 2009, with the weights already normalized).

results.title: Tajima's $\theta_\pi$ in site frequency spectrum form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Tajima's `θ_π` in its SFS form `∑_i i (n - i) ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `(n - i) / C(n,2)`).

reading_title.source: Tajima's $\theta_\pi$ in site frequency spectrum form

results.title: Fay and Wu's $\theta_H$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fay & Wu's `θ_H = ∑_i i² ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `i / C(n,2)`).

results.title: Fay and Wu's H statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fay & Wu's `H = θ_π - θ_H` (Fay & Wu 2000).

results.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The numerator `S - a₁ ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `D` with an outgroup, where `S = ∑_i ξ_i` and the external-branch mutations are the derived singletons `ξ₁` (Fu & Li 1993).

results.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The numerator `θ_π - ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `F` with an outgroup (Fu & Li 1993), with `θ_π` in its SFS form.

results.title: Achaz's unbiasedness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Achaz's unbiasedness (Achaz 2009): if `E ξ_i = θ / i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 1` (the constant-size spectrum, `SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`), every weighted estimator with `∑_i ω_i = 1` has mean `θ`.

results.title: Fay and Wu's H has mean zero at constant size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fay & Wu's `H` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).

results.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D has mean zero at constant size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The numerator of Fu & Li's `D` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).

results.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F has mean zero at constant size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The numerator of Fu & Li's `F` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).

results.title: Achaz's estimator is unbiased under Kingman's coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Achaz's unbiasedness under Kingman's coalescent, with the hypotheses of `SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`.

results.title: Cumulative coalescence intensity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The cumulative coalescence intensity `R(s) = ∫_0^s 1/η` of a relative population-size function `η` (pairs coalesce at rate `1/η(s)` at time `s` before the present). Meaningful for positive `η` with `1/η` locally integrable.

results.title: Expected time to the first coalescence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected time to the first coalescence among `m` lineages, `c_m = ∫_0^∞ exp(-C(m,2) R(s)) ds`, in a population of relative size `η` (Bhaskar & Song's `E[T_{m,m}]`). When the integrand is not integrable (for example `η ≡ 0`), this is Lean's junk value `0`; for piecewise-constant histories it is integrable (`choose_two_mul_firstCoalMean`).

results.title: Piecewise-constant population-size history
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A piecewise-constant population-size history with `K` pieces: piece `j < K` starts at time `start j` (backward from the present, `start 0 = 0`, strictly increasing) and has relative size `size j > 0`; the last piece extends to infinity. Adjacent pieces may have equal sizes, so this also covers histories with fewer than `K` distinct pieces. Values at indices `j ≥ K` are unused. The case `K = 0` is degenerate (its…

results.title: Size function of a piecewise-constant history
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The population-size function of a piecewise-constant history: at time `s ≥ 0` it is the size of the piece `j` with `start j ≤ s < start (j + 1)` (the last piece has no end). Equal to `0` for `s < 0` (junk; only `s ≥ 0` is meaningful).

results.title: Monotonicity of piece start times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The start times are monotone on the pieces.

results.title: Nonnegativity of piece start times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every piece starts at a nonnegative time.

results.title: Size function on a piece equals the piece size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On piece `j` the size function equals `size j`.

results.title: Cumulative rate is affine on each piece
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On piece `j` (including its right end), `1 / sizeFn` is integrable on `[0, s]` and the cumulative rate is affine: `R(s) = R(start j) + (s - start j) / size j`.

results.title: Closed form of the first-coalescence times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a history with `K ≥ 1` pieces and `m ≥ 2`, writing `a = C(m,2)` and `R = cumRate h.sizeFn`, `a c_m = size 0 + ∑_{j=1}^{K-1} (size j - size (j-1)) exp(-a R(start j))`. In particular the integral defining `c_m` converges.

results.title: Every nonnegative time lies in some piece
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every time `s ≥ 0` lies in some piece.

results.title: Positivity of the piecewise size function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The size function is positive on `[0, ∞)`.

results.title: Coalescent-time breakpoints are strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The coalescent-time breakpoints `R(start j)` are strictly increasing.

results.title: Dual history in coalescent time
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dual history in coalescent time: piece `j` starts at `R(start j)` and has size `1 / size j`.

results.title: Size function is the inverse of the dual size in coalescent time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The size at time `s` is the inverse of the dual history's size at coalescent time `R(s)`.

results.title: Dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate.

results.title: Cumulative rate is strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The cumulative rate is strictly increasing on `[0, ∞)`.

results.title: Bhaskar–Song identifiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Bhaskar–Song identifiability (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7, "determined" half, stated for the first-coalescence times): two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose expected first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ n`, with `n ≥ 2K`, have the same population size at every time `s ≥ 0`. The proof writes `C(m,2) c_m` as an exponential sum in `C(m,2)` over at most `2K - 1` rates…

results.title: Tightness of `n ≥ 2K`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Tightness of `n ≥ 2K` (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7): for every `K ≥ 2` there are two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose sizes differ at some time `s ≥ 0` but whose first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ 2K - 1`; so `sizeFn_eq_of_firstCoalMean_eq` fails for `n = 2K - 1`. The construction is explicit: with `z = 2^{-C(m,2)}`, the two histories have coalescent-time breakpoints…

results.title: Measurability of the piecewise size function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The size function is measurable.

results.title: Size function lies between the extreme piece sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On `[0, ∞)` the size function lies between the smallest and the largest piece size.

results.title: Size function is locally constant to the right
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The size function is constant on an interval to the right of every `s ≥ 0`.

results.title: Distinct two-piece histories with equal first-coalescence times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The two-piece case of `exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`.

results.title: First-coalescence times depend only on sizes at nonnegative times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Only the values on `[0, ∞)` enter the first-coalescence times.

results.title: Non-identifiability from a bounded sample size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every `n` there are two measurable population-size functions, bounded between positive constants and different on a set of positive measure in `[0, ∞)`, with the same `c_m` for `2 ≤ m ≤ n` (two `(n + 2)`-piece histories from `PiecewiseHistory.exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`, extended to `s < 0` by their size at `0`). This is the finite-sample shape of the statement of Myers, Fefferman & Patterson (2008);…

results.title: Non-identifiability of general histories
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Non-identifiability of general histories (Myers, Fefferman & Patterson 2008): there are two measurable population-size functions, bounded between positive constants, that differ on a set of positive Lebesgue measure in `[0, ∞)` and have the same expected first-coalescence time `c_m` for every `m ≥ 2` (hence the same expected SFS for every sample size).
